result:
Done. The change request is implemented end to end and committed.

## What changed

**New structured names.** Clients now carry `firstName` and `lastName`. Create/update accept them, and every client response includes both (plus the joined full `name`, kept for backward compatibility).

**Legacy `name` still works.** Writes that send a single `name` are split on the last space — everything before is the first name, the last word is the last name, a single word becomes just the last name (empty first name). Both the create and update paths honor this, and a partial update (e.g. `firstName` only) keeps the untouched part and recomputes the full name.

**Startup migration.** A new SQL migration (`006-client-name-parts.sql`) adds `first_name`/`last_name` columns; `server.js` then backfills any pre-split records in place. It's idempotent (only touches rows still missing both parts), so restarts are no-ops.

**Report shows current name.** The receivables query now joins `customers` and derives each row's name from the client's *current* first/last name (`TRIM(first || ' ' || last)`) instead of the stale order-time snapshot — verified by renaming a client after an order was issued and seeing the new name in the report.

## Files touched
- `src/lib/names.js` (new) — `splitName` / `fullName` helpers
- `src/db/migrations/006-client-name-parts.sql` (new)
- `src/schemas/customer.schema.js`, `src/routes/clients.routes.js`, `src/services/customers.service.js`, `src/repositories/customers.repo.js`, `src/repositories/orders.repo.js`, `src/server.js`

All 140 existing tests pass, and `typecheck` + `lint` are clean. The layering conventions were preserved (SQL only in repos; validation via `validate()` plus the cross-field name check in the route/service, matching the existing empty-body pattern).
